# Depot shift guide

## Morning checks

Walk the racks and log anything broken on the tablet.

## Charging

Batteries under forty percent go on the wall chargers.

## Repairs

Most of the shift goes here. Bikes reach the bench in the order they were
logged. That order is usually fine. A queue of six flat tyres can still
hide one bike with a cracked frame that shouldn't go back out, so look down
the whole list before you pick anything up. Frames and brakes come first,
then gears, then tyres and baskets. If a part is out of stock, hang a red
tag on the handlebars and park the bike in the back row. Don't try to
borrow the part from another bike. We tried that for a month last year and
ended up with two half-working bikes for every broken one, plus a stock
count that no longer matched the shelves. The supplier usually delivers on
Tuesdays and Fridays. Whoever is on shift that day fits the waiting parts
before starting on new repairs.

## Handover

Count the racks before you leave and phone the duty manager about anything
missing.
